narrative: 大多数说话镜头的拍摄都落在这个角度上。你能看到两只眼睛、鼻梁，以及一侧向后退去的脸颊，头骨的体积感足够打光，也足够让人读出倾听的状态。
它之所以有用，是因为既能塑造头部的立体感，又能沿着自然的视线与画外的对话对象保持连接。如果你想要硬币般的侧脸效果，用侧面镜头（Profile）；如果要对着镜头忏悔，用打破第四面墙（Fourth Wall）——这两种情况下四分之三侧面都不是合适的工具。
它也不是一个高度概念：你可以在平视（Eye Level）、低角度（Low Angle）或高角度（High Angle）下拍摄四分之三侧面。这个名字指的是水平偏转角，而不是俯仰角。
how: 把摄影机放在偏离拍摄对象鼻子方向大约30到50度的位置。保留两只眼球都可见；远侧的耳朵最多只遮住一小部分。
50mm到85mm的焦段能稳定地容纳头部，不会拉伸近侧的眼睛。根据窄面光（Short Lighting）或宽面光（Broad Lighting）的需要，从远侧或近侧布置主光；正是这个角度赋予了面部的层次感。
提示词：three-quarter angle, face turned about 45 degrees, both eyes, classic portrait dimensionality.
when: 当一张脸既需要立体感、又必须属于场景的一部分时，把它当作叙事性肖像镜头的默认选择。具体场景：餐馆里的单人镜头，身体转开45度，视线投向画面左侧的对话对象，两只眼睛都清晰锐利。
如果隐藏情绪才是重点，就不要用它；转到侧面镜头（Profile）。
vs: 侧面镜头（Profile）是90度、一只耳朵、远侧眼睛消失。平视（Eye Level）说的是摄影机的高度；四分之三侧面说的是头部转动的角度。
过肩镜头（Over-the-Shoulder Coverage）常常在近处肩膀占据画面的同时，让远处的脸保持四分之三侧面。完全正对镜头的注视是打破第四面墙（Fourth Wall）或访谈镜头（Interview）的视线，而不是四分之三侧面。
examples_film: 《盗火线》（Heat）的餐馆对峙戏让两张脸都保持四分之三侧面，使两人都保留完整的头部体积感，同时画面方向感保持清晰。从制片厂时代的特写到客厅剧情片，经典肖像拍摄都用同样的45度转角来塑造脸颊的立体感。
要借鉴的是这个偏转角度和两只可见的眼睛，而不是照搬那个卡座场景。
mistakes: 最容易混淆的错误对象是侧面镜头（Profile，转得太多）或护照照片式的正脸（转得太少）。辨别标志：远侧眼睛消失，或者两只耳朵都同样可见。
修正方法：角度保持在大约45度，两只眼球都可见，一只耳朵占主导。另一种常见错误是把低角度（Low Angle）误称为四分之三侧面。
俯仰角不等于偏转角；两者都要说清楚。

faq.q: 电影中的四分之三侧面是什么？
faq.a: 四分之三侧面把脸相对摄影机转动大约45度。两只眼睛都保持可见，远侧脸颊向后退去，这是叙事性肖像镜头的默认拍法。

faq.q: 四分之三侧面 vs 侧面镜头
faq.a: 四分之三侧面保留两只眼睛和一侧后退的脸颊。侧面镜头是90度的正侧面：一只耳朵，鼻子呈一条线，远侧眼睛被遮挡。

faq.q: 什么时候该用四分之三侧面？
faq.a: 用于大多数仍需与画外对话对象保持连接的说话肖像镜头。若要保留隐秘感，用侧面镜头；若要让观众介入，就用看向镜头的方式。

faq.q: 如何为AI图像或视频撰写四分之三侧面的提示词？
faq.a: 写法：Three-quarter angle on [Subject], face turned about 45 degrees, both eyes visible, far cheek receding. 摄影机高度要单独说明。既不是侧面镜头，也不是看向镜头。

narrative: Most coverage of a talking face lives here. You see both eyes, the bridge of the nose, and a cheek going away, which is enough skull to light and enough access to read a listen.

It is useful because it models the head and still connects to an offscreen partner along a natural eyeline. It is the wrong tool when you want a coin (use Profile) or a confession into the taking lens (use Fourth Wall).
It is also not a height: you can shoot three-quarter from Eye Level, Low Angle, or High Angle. The name is yaw, not tilt.
how: Place the camera about 30 to 50 degrees off the subject's nose. Keep both irises; hide only a sliver of the far ear if any.
A 50mm to 85mm holds the head without stretching the near eye. Key from the far or near side depending on short or broad lighting; the angle is what gives the planes.
Prompt: three-quarter angle, face turned about 45 degrees, both eyes, classic portrait dimensionality.
when: Use it as the default narrative portrait when a face must have volume and still belong to a scene. Concrete beat: a diner single, body open 45 degrees, eyeline to the partner off left, both eyes sharp.
Do not use it when concealment is the point; rotate to Profile.
vs: Profile is 90 degrees, one ear, far eye gone. Eye Level is how high the camera sits; three-quarter is how the head is turned.
Over-the-Shoulder Coverage often holds a three-quarter far face with a near shoulder chewing the frame. A full-front look into lens is Fourth Wall or an Interview eyeline, not three-quarter.
examples_film: Heat 's diner encounter parks two faces in three-quarter so each man remains a full head while screen direction stays clean. Classical portrait coverage from studio-era close-ups through drawing-room films uses the same 45-degree turn to model a cheek.
Borrow the yaw and the two eyes, not a copied booth.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is Profile (too much turn) or a passport front (too little). Tell: far eye gone, or both ears equally seen.
Fix: about 45 degrees, both irises, one ear dominant. The other failure is calling a Low Angle a three-quarter.
Pitch is not yaw; say both.

faq.q: What is a three-quarter angle in film?
faq.a: A three-quarter angle turns the face about 45 degrees to camera. Both eyes stay visible and the far cheek recedes, which is the default narrative portrait.
Three-quarter keeps both eyes and a receding cheek. Profile is a 90-degree side view: one ear, nose as a line, far eye hidden.

faq.q: When should I use a three-quarter angle?
faq.a: Use it for most talking portraits that still need a connection to an offscreen partner. Use profile to withhold, or a look into lens to admit the audience.

faq.q: How do I prompt a three-quarter angle for AI image or video?
faq.a: Write: Three-quarter angle on [Subject], face turned about 45 degrees, both eyes visible, far cheek receding. Name camera height separately. Not profile, not into the lens.
